597084.old: The reagent that attaches to the ring is an electrophile ("electron-lover"): an electron-poor species that is attracted to the electron-rich ring. On its own Br2 is not a strong enough electrophile, which is why benzene gives no reaction in the bromine test. The catalyst (FeBr3 for bromine, H2SO4 for nitric acid) makes the reagent a much stronger electrophile, and the substitution proceeds.
597084.new: On its own Br<sub>2</sub> is not reactive enough to substitute on the ring, which is why benzene gives no reaction in the bromine test. The catalyst (FeBr<sub>3</sub> for bromine, H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> for nitric acid) makes the reagent reactive enough, and the substitution proceeds.
